Day 7 · A day in the Coffee Valley of the State of Rio de Janeiro, a journey into Brazil’s past. The road runs through rolling hills, palms, bamboo and eucalyptus to a historic coffee fazenda, where Brazil’s wealth was once born: here lived the coffee barons who, in the 19th century, made Brazil the world’s biggest coffee producer. Their estates were palaces, with high ceilings, grand salons, crystal and European silver, surrounded by endless coffee plantations, a world as rich as it was harsh, built on the labour of enslaved people. The story of “The Slave Isaura”, the famous novel by Bernardo Guimarães that became a legendary Brazilian TV series, was filmed in fazendas like this one.

See the old machines used to roast the beans, the drying patios and the barns, then enjoy a tasting of coffee grown on the estate, as a master explains how the sun shapes the taste of the beans. A walk through the gardens, with bougainvillea, jasmine, mango trees, lakes and white herons, completes a day that reveals another side of Brazil: not only beaches and samba, but roots and memories. Return to Rio.
